subject: Culture
title: Military Uniforms
description: A fast breakdown of Military Uniforms for builders.

hook.text: Before the 1600s, armies wore whatever they owned. Friendly fire was common because nobody could tell sides apart.

buildup.text: Matching uniforms emerged for identification, discipline, and unity. Wearing the same thing builds group cohesion.

discovery.text: Camouflage wasn't adopted until World War I. Before that, armies chose bright colors to intimidate.

twist.text: The Maasai wore red into battle to symbolize blood and bravery. Color choice has always been strategic, not aesthetic.

climax.text: Modern special forces wear no insignia. In covert warfare, anonymity is the most powerful uniform.

punchline.text: Uniforms say 'us versus them' without a single word.

quiz.question: When was camouflage first widely adopted?
